Perfect forecasting of price-responsive EV load makes time-of- use and real-time price bulk power system production cost savings similar to those of DLC with up to 27% to 45% or more light-duty vehicles participating, where the lower bound is observed when EV charging is scheduled over an entire week, and the upper bound corresponds to scheduling EV charging within individual sessions (Figure ES-1). Additionally, flattening price- response to time-of-use rates enables production cost savings with light-duty vehicle time-of-use participation up to 45% for both within-week and within-session scheduling, and this could be value-competitive with DLC over that full range if the incremental costs of DLC are more than $10–30/vehicle-yr. This increase in effective price-responsive EVMC represents an additional 3 to 5 percentage points of production cost savings achievable without DLC. These results are based on simulations of an envisioned New England power system in which 84% of annual within-system generation is sourced from wind, solar, biomass, hydropower, and nuclear generators. Although we would expect the quantitative results to vary from system to system and with changes to the EV modeling methods, we expect the qualitative results to stand, that is, with accurate forecasting and response flattening, time-of-use EVMC can be value- competitive with DLC managed charging approaches with active participation levels approaching or around up to half of the light-duty vehicle fleet. vi This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Perfect-foresight preserves positive value for price-responsive, within-session EVMC applied to up to 45% of the light- duty vehicle (LDV) fleet. Time-of-use (TOU) savings are only tens of dollars per vehicle-year lower than DLC for all modeled LDV participation shares, suggesting additional costs of DLC should not exceed tens of dollars per vehicle- year for bulk power system EVMC.
